text: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize pathogens and help prevent infection or severe disease.
source: World Health Organization

text: Sudden one-sided weakness, confusion, speech trouble, vision trouble, balance trouble, or a severe headache can signal stroke and needs emergency care.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Antibiotics do not treat viruses; unnecessary use can cause side effects and antimicrobial resistance.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Suspected heart attack requires an immediate call to emergency services; delaying care can cause serious harm.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Insulin helps glucose move from blood into cells for energy and helps store glucose for later use.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Read over-the-counter medicine labels, follow directions, check active ingredients, and ask a pharmacist or doctor when unsure.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Soap and water or alcohol-based sanitizer helps remove germs; hands should be cleaned at important times.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so measurement is important; uncontrolled pressure raises cardiovascular risk.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Healthy eating, physical activity, and healthy weight can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Adequate sleep supports physical health, emotional well-being, attention, and memory.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Regular activity can improve heart health, strengthen bones and muscles, support mental health, and reduce chronic disease risk.
source: World Health Organization

text: Dehydration occurs when fluid loss exceeds intake; thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, or confusion can occur.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: Food allergy symptoms can include hives, swelling, vomiting, wheezing, or breathing difficulty; severe reactions need emergency care.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: Asthma can cause wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and coughing; action plans and prescribed treatments help manage it.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease commonly affecting the lungs and spreads through air from active pulmonary disease.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Malaria is caused by parasites transmitted by infected mosquitoes; suspected malaria needs prompt evaluation.
source: World Health Organization

text: Mental health supports coping and relationships; mental health conditions are common and treatable.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Depression can involve persistent low mood or loss of interest and changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration.
source: National Institute of Mental Health

text: Ultraviolet radiation causes skin cancer; shade, protective clothing, and sunscreen reduce exposure.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Quitting smoking lowers cancer, heart disease, stroke, and respiratory disease risk; counseling and medicines can help.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Alcohol-related health risks vary by amount and pattern; drinking less generally reduces risk.
source: World Health Organization

text: High LDL cholesterol can contribute to artery plaque and cardiovascular risk; testing and clinician assessment guide care.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Early chronic kidney disease may have no symptoms; blood and urine tests can detect kidney damage or reduced function.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: Some vaccines are recommended during pregnancy while others may be delayed; decisions should follow current clinical guidance.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Antimicrobial resistance occurs when germs no longer respond to medicines; appropriate use helps slow resistance.
source: World Health Organization

text: Concussion is a traumatic brain injury; worsening symptoms or danger signs require urgent medical evaluation.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Cool a burn under cool running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible; urgent care is needed for large, deep, facial, genital, chemical, or electrical burns.
source: National Health Service

text: Suspected poisoning requires an immediate call to a poison control center; treatment depends on the type of poison.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: Take medicines as directed on the label or by a doctor or pharmacist; ask a healthcare professional when instructions are unclear.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Diagnostic tests help providers investigate symptoms, detect disease, and make care decisions; the appropriate test depends on the health problem being assessed.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: WHO states that vaccines train the immune system to create antibodies; vaccines contain killed or weakened germs and do not cause the diseases they prevent.
source: World Health Organization

text: WHO reports that immunization prevents an estimated 3.5 million to 5 million deaths each year.
source: World Health Organization

text: Sudden trouble with balance, vision, facial or limb strength, speech, or a severe unexplained headache can be a stroke warning sign.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: The CDC advises calling 911 immediately for suspected stroke; fast treatment can reduce the brain damage a stroke causes.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Antibiotics treat some infections caused by bacteria, but some bacterial infections improve without antibiotics; a clinician should decide whether they are needed.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC advises taking an antibiotic exactly as prescribed, not sharing it, and not saving it for a future illness.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: A heart attack occurs when blood flow carrying oxygen to part of the heart muscle becomes blocked; without rapid restoration of blood flow, heart muscle can begin to die.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: A heart attack is a life-threatening medical emergency requiring immediate treatment; possible symptoms include chest or upper-body pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, sweating, and nausea.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: People with type 1 diabetes need insulin because their pancreas does not make insulin; dosing is needed across the day, including around food and drink.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: The diabetes medicine selected depends on diabetes type and how well the medicine controls blood glucose; other health conditions and personal circumstances can also matter.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: CDC advises checking active ingredients in prescription and over-the-counter medicines to avoid giving or taking two products with the same ingredient.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: If medicine label instructions are unclear, CDC advises asking a pharmacist or doctor before taking the medicine.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC recommends scrubbing hands with soap for at least 20 seconds, then rinsing them under clean running water.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: When soap and water are not readily available, CDC recommends using hand sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Blood pressure measures the force of blood flow against artery walls; high blood pressure means this force is often too high.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: The systolic blood pressure number reflects pressure when the heart pumps; the diastolic number reflects pressure between beats when the heart relaxes.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Prediabetes often has no signs, so a blood test is needed to find out whether someone has it.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC describes weight loss, healthy eating, and more physical activity as lifestyle changes that can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes in people with prediabetes.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC says recommended sleep duration changes with age; adults aged 18 to 60 should get at least seven hours per day.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC associates getting enough sleep with better attention and memory, improved mood, and lower risk of some chronic conditions and motor-vehicle injuries.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: WHO defines physical activity as bodily movement produced by skeletal muscles that requires energy expenditure; it includes movement during leisure, transport, work, and household activities.
source: World Health Organization

text: WHO reports that regular physical activity benefits physical and mental health, while inactivity increases the risk of noncommunicable diseases and other poor health outcomes.
source: World Health Organization

text: Dehydration occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in and does not have enough fluid to function properly.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: MedlinePlus lists thirst, dry mouth, reduced urination, dark urine, tiredness, and dizziness among symptoms of dehydration in adults.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: A food allergy is an immune-system reaction to a food; food intolerance is different and is not an immune-system reaction.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: MedlinePlus notes that food-allergy reactions are often mild but can sometimes be serious or life-threatening.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: Asthma is a chronic condition in which airways can become inflamed and narrowed, making it harder for air to flow during breathing.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: NHLBI states there is no cure for asthma, but treatment and an asthma action plan can help manage the condition.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

text: Inactive tuberculosis infection usually causes no symptoms, and people with inactive TB do not spread TB to others.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: People with active TB disease may feel sick and may spread TB germs; untreated active TB disease can be fatal.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Malaria is caused by parasites and is mostly transmitted to people through bites from infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
source: World Health Organization

text: Fever, headache, and chills are common early malaria symptoms; WHO says early testing is important because symptoms can resemble other febrile illnesses.
source: World Health Organization

text: CDC describes mental health as including emotional, psychological, and social well-being, and notes that it is closely linked to physical health.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC says individual, family, community, and societal factors can influence mental health; help is available for people experiencing mental distress.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Depression can cause severe symptoms that affect feelings, thinking, and daily activities such as sleeping, eating, or working.
source: National Institute of Mental Health

text: NIMH reports that depression is linked to other health conditions, including heart disease and diabetes, and can be associated with suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
source: National Institute of Mental Health

text: Most skin cancers are caused by excessive ultraviolet exposure; UV rays can damage skin cells and come from both sunlight and tanning beds.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC says UV rays can reach people on cloudy or cool days and can reflect off water, cement, sand, and snow; it advises sun protection when the UV Index is 3 or higher.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Quitting smoking benefits health at any age, regardless of how long or how much a person has smoked.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC says quitting smoking reduces the risk of premature death and many adverse outcomes, including cardiovascular disease, COPD, cancer, and poor reproductive outcomes.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: WHO describes ethanol in alcoholic beverages as a psychoactive and toxic substance with dependence-producing properties.
source: World Health Organization

text: WHO reports that alcohol can pose health risks even at low consumption levels, while most alcohol-related harm comes from heavy episodic or continuous consumption.
source: World Health Organization

text: High LDL cholesterol can lead to plaque buildup in arteries and increase the risk of heart disease or stroke.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC identifies HDL as the type of cholesterol for which higher levels can lower heart disease and stroke risk; a lipid panel checks cholesterol and triglycerides.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: Early kidney disease usually has no symptoms, so testing is needed to assess kidney function.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: NIDDK describes a blood GFR test and a urine albumin test as tests providers use to check for kidney disease; people with diabetes should be checked every year.
source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

text: NHS guidance says inactivated seasonal flu and whooping cough vaccines are recommended during pregnancy in the UK to help protect the pregnant person and baby.
source: National Health Service

text: NHS explains that antibodies produced after whooping cough vaccination in pregnancy pass to the baby and help protect the baby before their own vaccination course begins.
source: National Health Service

text: Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites do not respond to antimicrobial medicines, making infections harder or sometimes impossible to treat.
source: World Health Organization

text: WHO identifies misuse and overuse of antimicrobials as drivers of the development and spread of drug-resistant pathogens.
source: World Health Organization

text: Symptoms of mild traumatic brain injury or concussion can appear immediately or hours or days after an injury, and symptoms differ among people.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC advises immediate emergency care for danger signs after concussion, including a worsening headache, repeated vomiting, weakness, seizures, slurred speech, or unusual behavior.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: NHS first-aid guidance says to cool a burn or scald under cool running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible.
source: National Health Service

text: NHS advises urgent emergency care for burns that are very large or deep, affect the face or genitals, or are caused by chemicals or electricity.
source: National Health Service

text: A substance can be poisonous if too much is taken, and poisoning can occur through swallowing, inhaling, injection, or absorption through the skin.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: For suspected poisoning in the United States, MedlinePlus advises contacting the local poison control center immediately; treatment depends on the substance involved.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: CDC suggests using reminders such as timers or apps to help take medicines on time and following the label or instructions from a doctor or pharmacist.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: CDC advises keeping a list of medicines, vitamins, and supplements and making sure a doctor knows about everything being taken.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text: MedlinePlus says medical tests can help detect a condition, determine a diagnosis, plan treatment, and check whether treatment is working.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)

text: MedlinePlus explains that a doctor may order tests during a routine checkup, to investigate specific diseases or disorders, or to monitor health over time.
source: National Library of Medicine (MedlinePlus)
